reference.build: Nix .#llama-cpp-flint-reference (.devops/nix/llama-cpp-reference.nix): nixpkgs llama-cpp with ROCm for gfx1151, LLAMA_HIP_UMA, ROCm 7.2.3, AMD clang 22

gufo.build: nix build (production package; ROCm 7.2.3, AMD clang 22, GCC 15.3.0)

scope: Benchmark and qualification evidence for the initial Flint integration.

benchmarks-2026-10-23.scope: Complete card: single-ar d0-131072, multi-ar C1/2/4/6/8, cold loading at capacity 262144, both memory rows; Gufo and llama.cpp.
benchmarks-2026-10-23.measurement: One warmed sample per point (multi-ar: three cohorts), greedy seed 1, HTTP on both sides, fresh server per sweep/concurrency, Nix builds on both sides, idle desktop.

conditions.powerProfile: performance (power-profiles-daemon, amd_pstate; no ACPI platform profile)
conditions.backgroundGpu: gpu_busy_percent 0 before, between and after; no other DRM client above 1.3% of the graphics engine

benchmarks-2026-10-23.loadingMethod: POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED on the GGUF before each launch; fincore verified zero resident pages. Runtime libraries may be warm.
benchmarks-2026-10-23.quality: Prompt/cache counts identical across servers (d131072 frontier one token apart). Every timed Gufo completion hashes dede3fc3..., as in the earlier host-compiler card.

controls.terminalContention: An identical run beside a terminal using about 25% of the graphics engine was 2-7% slower on both engines (Gufo d0 2211.31 pp / 65.46 tg, C8 252.93).
controls.unpinnedLlamaCpp: The unpinned ROCm build of llama.cpp 970b51ce used for the earlier card reproduces it on the idle desktop: d0/64K/128K pp 1659.2/566.33/316.93, tg 53.58/36.25/27.57.
controls.toolchain: Paired native gufo bench, Nix vs host compiler: -1 to -2.7% prefill, +-0.6% decode (Q4 C8 -1.8%); completion hashes identical.
